title: Bounded outward walk
statement: For the designated machine with parameter $K_0$, oracle $\mathrm{orc}:\{0,\ldots,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$, input $x$, and natural bounds $B,P$, let $st$ be a memory access site, $k$ a natural number, $S$ a machine state, $M:\mathbb Z\to\{0,1\}$ a memory marking, and $p\in\mathbb Z$. If $S.T=k$, every register of $S$ is at most $B$, $S.T_2+k\le B$, $0\le p$, and $p+k\le P$, then the machine has a finite run from the outward-walk configuration at $st$, with state $S$, marking $M$, and head position $p$, to the memory-operation configuration at $st$, with the same marking, head position $p+k$, and state obtained by setting $T$ to zero and $T_2$ to $S.T_2+k$, leaving every other state component unchanged. Every configuration strictly before the endpoint satisfies the register-instruction precondition, has all registers at most $B$, and has memory head between $0$ and $P$.
hypotheses_covered: Natural parameter $K_0$ and the designated machine with that parameter
Oracle from four indices and Boolean strings to Booleans
Integer head position $p$ with $0\le p$ and $p+k\le P$
Every register of $S$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Fix the designated machine, oracle, input, and natural bounds $B,P$. For every memory
access site $st$, walk length $k$, register state $S$, marking $M:\mathbb
Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and head position $p$, suppose $S.T=k$, every
register of $S$ is at most $B$, $S.T2+k\le B$, $0\le p$, and $p+k\le P$. Then the
machine can run from the outward-walk configuration at $st$ with state $S$, marking $M$,
and head $p$, to the memory-operation configuration at $st$ with the same marking, state
$S$ except that $T$ is set to zero and $T2$ to $S.T2+k$, and head position $p+k$. Every
configuration before the endpoint satisfies the guard: its register-instruction
precondition holds and all register values are at most $B$, while its memory head lies
between $0$ and $P$.
